issues.legal_issue: A stepchild is not included among the children who inherit first from a female Hindu who dies intestate, and cannot share in that category simultaneously with her own child.
material_facts: A woman died intestate leaving property that had devolved to her from her husband.
She was survived by her son from that husband and by the son of her husband’s other wife, who claimed a share alongside her son.
The lower courts held that the woman’s own son was entitled to the property.
issues.conclusion: The word “sons” in section 15(1)(a) does not include a step-son. A step-son is an heir of the husband under section 15(1)(b), and does not share with the deceased woman’s own children under section 15(1)(a). The son of the deceased woman was therefore entitled to the property in this case.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 15(1)(a) and 16 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, heirs in an earlier entry take before heirs in a later entry, and heirs within the same entry take simultaneously. “Sons” in section 15(1)(a) includes sons born to the woman by the same or different husbands, illegitimate sons deemed related to their mother under section 3(j), adopted sons, and the children of predeceased sons; it does not include step-sons. The Court reasoned that this accords with the prior Hindu law rule giving a woman’s own son precedence over a step-son, and that a departure from that rule would have required express language. It approved Mallappa Fakirappa Sanna Nagashetti v. Shivappa, Rama Ananda Patil v. Appa Bhima Redekar, Gumam Singh v. Smt. Ass Kaur, and Smt. Kishori Bala Mondal v. Tribhanga Mondal, and overruled Ram Katori v. Prakash Wati.

predicates.female_intestate_succession_case: A female Hindu died without a will and the dispute concerns succession to her estate.
predicates.claimant_is_spouse_child_from_other_unio: A claimant is the child of the deceased woman’s spouse from another union, rather than a child of the deceased woman.
predicates.deceased_has_qualifying_child: The deceased woman was survived by a child, including a child of a predeceased child, who qualifies in the first category of heirs.
predicates.stepchild_not_first_entry_heir: The stepchild is not treated as a first-category child heir who takes alongside the deceased woman’s own qualifying children.

issues.definition: When a female Hindu dies intestate, a surviving stepchild of her spouse is not a first-category child heir if the deceased woman has a qualifying child.
